newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat nearing complete emergence.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat nearing complete emergence.

text.p: Texas's winter wheat crop was more than 90 percent emerged during the week ended Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.

The report said warm, dry weather gave way to much cooler weather, bringing scattered rains to most areas of the state. Floods occurred and some livestock were lost to rapidly rising waters in the Hill Country.
Growth of small grain pastures was improving, and more cattle were moved onto wheat and oats for grazing.
Wheat planted 98 percent vs 95 week ago, 85 year ago, 85 on a five-year average.
Wheat emerged 92 percent vs 87 w/a, 66 y/a, 69 avg.
Wheat rated 76 percent of normal, vs 65 y/a.
Corn harvested 98 percent vs 97 w/a, 98 y/a, 99 avg.
Sorghum harvested 83 percent vs 75 w/a, 98 y/a, 99 avg.
Sorghum mature 100 percent vs 99 w/a, 93 y/a, 90 avg.
Cotton bolls opening 95 percent vs 91 w/a, 89 y/a, 89 avg.
Cotton harvested 41 percent vs 28 w/a, 48 y/a, 47 avg.
Cotton rated 69 percent good/excellent vs 50 w/a.
Pasture and range condition was rated 38 percent good to excellent, versus 46 percent at that level last week.
